To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total production cross section of W and Z bosons at the LHC are predicted to be 20.2 +/- 0.4 nb and 7.0 +/- 0.1 nb respectively, with the errors dominated by uncertainties in the gluon distribution and in the value of the strong coupling constant.

the total W/Z production cross sections at the LHC will be sensitive to the gluon and strong coupling, and to the sea quark distributions, and that the rapidity distributions will be sensitive to all these parameters, and also to the overall normalization of the parton distributions.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of W and Z bosons at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC), with particular emphasis on the dependence on the underlying parton distributions.
the study of the strong force at high energy, and in particular, the production of heavy particles at hadron colliders.
the production and detection of W bosons and the production of Z bosons at the LHC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
W and Z production will provide a very powerful test of our knowledge of partons and their evolution.
the LHC will allow us to make a precise measurement of the total W and Z production cross sections, which will allow us to test our understanding of the parton distributions, and the strong coupling.
the LHC is a golden opportunity to test the QCD parton distributions in the TeV region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the LHC energies, we can predict the total production cross section and rapidity distribution of the W and Z bosons to within 1% for the CTEQ6M PDF set.
the W and Z cross sections at LHC are very well predicted, but that there is some room for further improvement.
the parton distributions are not well known, and that the LHC will help us to learn more about them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for W production at the LHC, the gluon distribution dominates, and for Z production the sea quarks dominate.

the LHC will provide a powerful test of the parton distribution functions, and that it is therefore important to have a realistic assessment of the uncertainties in our knowledge of the parton distributions.
the total cross sections for W and Z boson production are sensitive to the shape of the gluon at low x, but that the shape of the sea quarks has little effect.
